key_insight: Physics-localized hyper-reduction accelerates coupled elastoplastic soil deformation and water-flow simulations while keeping displacement and pressure errors below 0.5%.
engineering_relevance: Faster repeated simulations could support calibration, uncertainty quantification and safety assessment of earthfill and tailings dams.
method: Build separate displacement and pore-pressure reduced bases using proper orthogonal decomposition.
Compute affine residual terms exactly and approximate nonlinear corrections with separate ECSW cubature rules for each balance equation.
Assemble the original FEniCSx variational forms only on selected elements concentrated in plastified and unsaturated zones.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D and 3D dams undergoing raising and consolidation, with material properties and raise height varied, achieved errors below 0.5% versus finite elements and speed-ups up to 43× and 77×, respectively.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the tested parameter ranges and loading scenarios is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: A hyper-reduction strategy for elastoplastic hydro-mechanical problems in partially saturated soil
